title: gen_fixtures.py: line wrapper splits escape pairs across line boundaries
description:
The Python fixture generator's yenc_line_wrap() function slices the pre-encoded byte stream at line_len=128 with no awareness of escape pairs. If an escaped byte's '=' character falls at encoded position 127 (the last byte of a line), the '=' ends up at the end of line N and the escaped byte starts line N+1. This is a valid (if uncommon) split-escape that the yEnc spec permits but that the Rust decoder currently mishandles (see MIME-592.19).

The existing fixtures happen not to trigger this: bytes(range(64)) and bytes(range(128)) have only one escaped byte (byte 19) which falls at encoded position 19, well inside the first 128-byte line. A payload with byte 19 at index 127 (e.g. [0]*127 + [19]) would trigger it.

Fix: update yenc_line_wrap() in gen_fixtures.py to be escape-pair-aware (don't split in the middle of a '=' + escaped pair), OR add a fixture that exercises the split-escape path to confirm the decoder handles it correctly after MIME-592.19 is fixed.
